patient.chief_complaint: Called 911 after sudden headache explosion while at home, found on floor by neighbor, vomiting
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Stevens is a 56-year-old white man with hypertension on verapamil, depression on sertraline, and active tobacco use who was found by his neighbor on the floor of his living room after she heard a crash. He had called her on the phone saying he had a sudden terrible headache and then dropped the phone. The neighbor arrived within 10 minutes and found him on the floor, alert but confused, with vomiting. EMS was called and he arrived in the ED 40 minutes later. He is now alert and oriented but in severe distress with a 10/10 headache. He has no recall of falling but believes he did not lose consciousness. He has marked nuchal rigidity and photophobia. His neighbor reports he had been feeling well earlier that day. He has been a heavy smoker for decades and drinks significant alcohol daily. He takes verapamil for hypertension — notably a calcium channel blocker that will interact with nimodipine. He also takes sertraline which prolongs QTc and may compound the neurogenic QTc prolongation seen in SAH. His blood pressure is severely elevated at presentation consistent with the catecholamine surge of SAH.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4; GCS 14 (confused initially, now 15); severe headache; photophobic
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: PERRL 3mm; EOM intact; mild papilledema suspected - fundoscopy borderline; no CN deficit
neurological_exam.additional: Marked nuchal rigidity; Kernig positive; Hunt-Hess Grade 2

findings.location: Basal cisterns and bilateral Sylvian fissures
findings.description: Thick subarachnoid blood in basal cisterns and bilateral Sylvian fissures

ct.impression: Subarachnoid hemorrhage Fisher grade 3. Heavy smoker and alcohol use increases cardiovascular risk. CTA urgently required.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: WBC 17.2 x10^9/L (H), Glucose 168 mg/dL (H), AST 62 U/L (H), GGT 184 U/L (H), Troponin I 0.28 ng/mL (H), BNP 214 pg/mL (H).

findings: QTc markedly prolonged 516 ms - combined neurogenic + sertraline effect

interactions: Verapamil + nimodipine: SIGNIFICANT - both calcium channel blockers, additive negative inotropy, hypotension, and bradycardia. Verapamil is non-dihydropyridine CCB with stronger cardiac effects.
Sertraline + nimodipine: QTc concern - sertraline prolongs QTc; combined with neurogenic QTc prolongation in SAH = torsades risk
warnings: HOLD verapamil immediately - additive CCB effect with nimodipine causes severe hypotension and bradycardia
HOLD sertraline - QTc 516 ms is critical threshold; sertraline exacerbates neurogenic QT prolongation
Monitor QTc before each nimodipine dose
Seek cardiology input for QT management
alternatives: Alternative BP agent after SAH: IV labetalol or hydralazine for acute BP management

findings.finding: Saccular aneurysm 5.8 x 5.2 mm - multilobulated, ruptured appearance

output.impression: AComA aneurysm 5.8 mm multilobulated consistent with ruptured aneurysm. Heavy smoker - smoking cessation critical. Urgent DSA and coiling.

output.wall_motion: Moderate apical and mid-ventricular hypokinesis - moderate Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
output.impression: Moderate Takotsubo cardiomyopathy EF 42%. High troponin and BNP correlate. Expected recovery 4-8 weeks.
recommended_actions: Cardiology urgently for QTc management + Takotsubo

output.impression: Mild-moderate bilateral ACA vasospasm consistent with AComA territory. Patient asymptomatic at this time. Continue nimodipine.

output.query: Alcohol withdrawal SAH management CIWA-Ar benzodiazepine safety

results.finding: Heavy alcohol use (>4-6 drinks daily) at high risk for withdrawal seizures 24-72h after last drink
CIWA-Ar protocol for alcohol withdrawal assessment - monitor every 4-8h
Benzodiazepines are first-line for alcohol withdrawal BUT cause sedation that can mask SAH neurological changes
Phenobarbital is alternative that also has anticonvulsant properties
SAH + alcohol withdrawal = complex; use lowest effective benzodiazepine dose with frequent neuro checks

output.summary: Patient drinks 4-6 beers daily - at risk for alcohol withdrawal seizures. CIWA-Ar monitoring every 4-8h. Use symptom-triggered benzodiazepine protocol but note sedation confounds neuro monitoring. Involve addiction medicine. Alcohol withdrawal seizures can also trigger SAH rebleeding.

output.query: QTc prolongation SAH sertraline management torsades prevention

results.finding: QTc >500 ms significantly increases torsades de pointes risk
Current QTc 516 ms - hold all QT-prolonging agents immediately
SAH neurogenic QT prolongation typically peaks days 2-4
Correct electrolytes: K+ >4.0, Mg2+ >2.0 for QT protection
Cardiology monitoring for QTc >500 ms in ICU setting

output.summary: QTc 516 ms requires immediate action: hold sertraline, correct K/Mg, cardiology consult. SAH neurogenic QT changes + sertraline = additive QT risk. ECG monitoring every 6-8h. Nimodipine can continue if QTc remains below 550 ms with monitoring.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from AComA aneurysm with critical QTc prolongation from combined neurogenic + sertraline effect (Hunt-Hess 2, Fisher 3)

differential.key_features: Subarachnoid not parenchymal pattern; CTA confirms aneurysm source
Saccular aneurysm on CTA; CSF bloody
No prior headache history; CT shows blood; aneurysm on CTA

optimal_actions.expected_finding: QTc 516 ms - neurogenic + sertraline combined effect
CIWA-Ar protocol; benzodiazepine caution with neuro monitoring

critical_actions: Hold verapamil immediately - additive CCB effect with nimodipine (hypotension + bradycardia)
Hold sertraline - QTc 516 ms is critically prolonged - torsades risk
QTc 516 ms: correct K+ >4.0, Mg2+ >2.0; cardiology consult
Monitor for alcohol withdrawal (4-6 beers daily) with CIWA-Ar protocol
Nimodipine 60 mg q4h x21 days after holding verapamil
contraindicated_actions: Do not continue verapamil with nimodipine - additive CCB effect
Do not continue sertraline with QTc 516 ms
Do not miss alcohol withdrawal risk in 4-6 beers/day patient
key_reasoning_points: Verapamil is a non-dihydropyridine CCB - combined with nimodipine causes severe hypotension and bradycardia
Sertraline prolongs QTc - combined with neurogenic SAH QT prolongation creates critical QTc 516 ms
QTc >500 ms = high torsades risk; hold all QT-prolonging agents
Heavy alcohol use (4-6 drinks/day) = withdrawal risk 24-72h after admission; CIWA-Ar monitoring
Active smoking is the strongest modifiable risk factor for aneurysm formation and rupture
